title: Blocker — why work is stalled, typed
_role: Every BLK-* validates against this. The `kind` field is the point: four situations with four different remedies must never be filed under one word.

kind.description: Exactly one. Selection ladder in taxonomy/blockers.md §3. Two pairs are the ones most often conflated and the conflation is expensive in both: (a) requires_better_simulation_accuracy vs requires_gpu_scale_simulation -- reading an accuracy problem as a scale problem buys more GPU for an answer that would still be wrong; (b) requires_external_collaboration vs requires_lower_experimental_cost -- where a repository excludes individuals by policy rather than price, no budget reaches it. `requires_future_technology` is a FALLBACK: use it only where nothing more specific fits.

statement_about.description: What KIND of thing this is a property of -- the architecture, the target, the operating regime, an instrument, the data. This is the human gloss that made the original register useful and it is kept alongside the enum, not replaced by it.

permanent.description: DERIVED from kind, never typed. Only fundamental_biological_limit is permanent.

owner.description: The file that owns the statement. This registry records where a fact lives; it does not restate it.

anchor.description: May be null: a memo that owns the statement in its entirety has no single section to point at, and inventing one would be a worse pointer than none.

retired_by_technology.description: DERIVED from each technology's `unblocks.blockers`, never typed -- otherwise the same edge would have two homes and could disagree with itself. A PERMANENT blocker must derive EMPTY: a fact about what the objects are is not waiting for anything, and putting one on a watch list wastes the watch.

retired_by_action.description: An action THIS PROGRAM can take that would retire the blocker, for blockers that no external capability unblocks. Discovered while building the register: a `scientific_uncertainty` blocker such as an absent specification is retired by stating the specification -- reasoning, not technology. Without this field the completeness invariant would have forced a fake technology dependency onto it, which is the opposite of what the taxonomy is for. Exactly the same distinction as the internal_work triggers that were sitting on a watch list.

inherited_by.description: DERIVED from the route register, never typed. Sorting by this length gives the portfolio's shape: a blocker on one route is a risk, a blocker on fifteen is the rate-limiter.

retired_by.description: DERIVED. Routes that ANSWER this blocker -- the portfolio's hedge against it.

families_held.description: DERIVED from the strategy of every route in `inherited_by`, never typed. The denominator `inherited_by` alone cannot supply: two blockers holding the SAME number of routes mean different things if one is concentrated in a single family and the other spans six -- the first is a route-selection problem, the second a program-level one.

reach.description: DERIVED from `families_held` by REACH_BANDS in systems_check.py. Named bands rather than a synthetic score on purpose: a 0-100 number would imply a precision the inputs do not carry, and the band is what a reader acts on.

resolution.description: DERIVED join: blocker -> technology -> forecast. The arrival bands live in the forecast register keyed by TECHNOLOGY, so 'when does this blocker lift' was a join every reader made by hand across two files. Computed here so a re-forecast moves it automatically and it can never disagree with registers/technologies.md. ⚠ A PERMANENT blocker resolves to class `permanent` with NO band -- [B1] already forbids a technology claiming to retire one, and a date printed beside one would reintroduce exactly that conflation.

class.description: Which KIND of thing would end this blocker: an advance we wait for (`forecast`), nothing at all (`permanent`), a person's decision (`decision`), an action we can take (`action`), or an unanalysed gap (`unforecast`, which [B2] fails the build on).

when.description: The governing `expected` band for class `forecast`; otherwise a word, never a date.

basis.description: The basis of the forecast supplying `when`, carried BESIDE the date because a band without it reads as a measurement. ⛔ It grades the technology's CURRENT STATE, NOT the date -- `evidence_based` means something has partly landed, which is compatible with a soft band whose own rationale is a pace argument. Read `confidence` for the date. Null for every non-`forecast` class.

confidence.description: The `expected` scenario's OWN confidence, from the forecast register. Printed beside `basis` and never derived from it: a strong `basis` next to a soft band is the shape most likely to be misread, which is exactly what happened to BLK-TERNARY-GEOMETRY (2026-08-08) -- `evidence_based` was read as evidence for 2027, when it is evidence that one arm of the capability already exists. Null for every non-`forecast` class.

per_tech.description: Per-technology bands, kept uncollapsed so the spread that the earliest-wins headline compresses stays visible.

evidence.description: What the blocker's existence rests on. A blocker asserted without evidence is an opinion holding down a route.

kind_history.description: REQUIRED when kind has ever changed. A reclassification changes what the program watches for, so it is a decision with reasoning, not a tidy-up.
